item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0021-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0021-E002","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The federal government's financial planning for the Climate and Transformation Fund totaled €211.8 billion through 2027 for investment in future technologies, production capacity, and climate protection in Germany.","notes":["The excerpt supports financial planning and intended investment areas, but not completed allocation or expenditure."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0021-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0021-E004","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The German government reaffirmed the goal of a world without nuclear weapons, identified the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty as Germany's central framework for nuclear disarmament and nonproliferation, developed concrete proposals with partners through the Stockholm Initiative to strengthen the treaty, and said it would remain in dialogue with Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons states about progress in nuclear disarmament.","notes":["The excerpt says Germany developed concrete proposals with partners; it does not explicitly say Germany supported Stockholm Initiative proposals."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0021-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The German government decided to procure F-35 aircraft to replace current aircraft used in NATO nuclear participation and maintained its position that credible NATO nuclear deterrence was necessary; Germany remained outside the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons because of tensions between the treaty's prohibitions and NATO obligations.","notes":["The excerpt supports the procurement decision, NATO nuclear participation, deterrence rationale, and non-accession; it does not explicitly state that Germany supported continued nuclear sharing."]}]}
